purpose: controlled positive control: run the same unchanged candidate on a clean card and again under sustained contention, to test whether the witnesses detect it and whether pairing absorbs it.

contentionMethod.how: a separate background process ran a sustained NPU multiply loop on the same device for 180 s, so the measured card was genuinely contended by a real process. This is a controlled experiment, not a fabricated observation: the contention was real, and the witnesses had to find it on their own.
contentionMethod.significance: This PID was briefly mistaken by the Lead for a third-party tenant. It was OURS. Recorded here so the attribution error does not survive in the evidence.

contendedRun.why: no quiet window was observed, so there is no reference showing that pairing cancels contention; contention was measured to shift the paired ratio by up to 2.05x on an unchanged candidate, so no performance verdict is made

finding1_pairingDoesNotAbsorbHeavyConten.claim: The paired protocol absorbs LIGHT contention (measured 3.3 percent earlier). It does NOT absorb sustained heavy contention: the paired ratio of an UNCHANGED candidate moved from 0.3224 to 0.6615, a factor of 2.05.
finding1_pairingDoesNotAbsorbHeavyConten.why: The two arms suffer unequally: the candidate is a 64-core SimtVF kernel, the vendor is a small heavily optimised kernel, so saturation of the AICore penalises them differently and the ratio does not cancel.
finding1_pairingDoesNotAbsorbHeavyConten.consequence: A run with no quiet window cannot decide performance. The protocol now returns RETEST in that case instead of attributing contention to the candidate.
finding1_pairingDoesNotAbsorbHeavyConten.correctedEarlierClaim: "paired ratio stable within +/-8 percent, neighbouring load shifts it 3.3 percent" holds for light load only.

finding2_canaryIsNotASensitiveDetector.claim: With AICore pinned at 99 percent for the whole run, the canary exceeded the 1.15 threshold in only 3 of 9 windows at 8192x4096 and 1 of 9 at 64x4096.
finding2_canaryIsNotASensitiveDetector.why: The canary measures a 0.06 ms kernel, so its own noise is the same order as the signal.
finding2_canaryIsNotASensitiveDetector.consequence: A canary INFLATION is strong positive evidence; a canary that does not inflate is WEAK evidence of quiet. The canary must never be used alone to justify a quiet label. Window-level contention is detected by the AICore trajectory (99 in all 9 windows here, correctly labelled).
finding2_canaryIsNotASensitiveDetector.costNote: Measured by the Lead: one canary costs ~0.64 s wall clock to arbitrate 0.004 ms of device time (160,000x). Repeating it per window is not affordable, so the sensitivity limit is accepted and recorded rather than papered over.

finding3_samplingRateIsSufficient.claim: samplingRateHz measured 1.16-3.88 with sparseWindows = 0, so the sparse guard did not misfire.
finding3_samplingRateIsSufficient.note: The Lead asked whether MIN_WITNESS_SAMPLES_PER_SECOND = 0.5 would mark every window sparse and make "quiet" unusable. It does not: the sampler is a run-level background thread and windows last about 1 s, so 5-8 samples land inside each window.

admissibility.quietRun: accept-genuine.json (12:53, no controlled load, all 10 windows quiet) is the performance evidence.
admissibility.contendedRun: contended-run.json is the witness validation experiment. It is NOT performance evidence and is judged RETEST by the current rule.
